maya_support: Hey — ACME reports a sudden vectors/sec drop on embeddings around 08:12 UTC. tokens/sec looks normal. They see GPU queue depth high and intermittent 429s. No recent model change on their side. Anyone seen this pattern before?

engbot: :rotating_light: Alert: vecs-rate-drop fired for customer=acme zone=us-west at 2025-02-12T08:12Z. Dash: https://dash.internal/redwood/alerts/vecs-rate-drop/1757777777

jordan_sre: Can you paste a minimal repro request and the model variant? Also need sample request_ids and the pod names from the affected time window.

maya_support: Sample: model=open-embed-v2-quant, batch_size=128, concurrency=40. Customer provided one request_id: req_5881fa. From pod logs around event: 

```
2025-02-12T08:11:58Z pod=embed-n0 rx=128 concurrency=40 queue_depth=72 vectors/sec=1200 tokens/sec=48000
2025-02-12T08:12:05Z pod=embed-n0 rx=128 concurrency=80 queue_depth=210 vectors/sec=320 tokens/sec=47000
2025-02-12T08:12:12Z pod=embed-n1 rx=64  concurrency=60 queue_depth=180 vectors/sec=300 tokens/sec=46500
```

eng_oncall: Good data. Two quick hypotheses: (1) batching window expansion + large concurrent retries causing big batches that thrash KV cache locks, (2) a quantized variant hitting a slow kernel under certain seq-len distributions. Try repro with a controlled curl that sends N=256 inputs with delay, and then with smaller batch_size to compare.

eng_oncall: Repro curl (safe, uses test token):
```
for i in $(seq 1 60); do \
  curl -sS -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_TEST" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
    -d '{"model":"open-embed-v2-quant","inputs":["test"]*128}'; sleep 0.1; \
done
```

maya_support: Ran quick test — smaller batches (batch_size=16) push vectors/sec back up to expected ~1500 per pod. Large batch runs show big queue_depth and throughput collapse. I also see auth retry spikes at the same time in their logs (a flurry of 401->retry entries). Could retries be amplifying the batch window?

alex_ml: 401 spikes could trigger client retries, raising concurrency and thus enlarging effective batch sizes. If the router aggregates by time window, unexpected concurrency spikes will create huge batches that break the optimized kernel path for quantized model. Can you check the batch_window_ms setting for this customer route?

maya_support: Route shows BATCH_WINDOW_MS=12ms, but we had a recent rollout that temporarily bumped default to 40ms for a different tenant; maybe the customer was routed to that hostpool. Here's quick rqs top output from node: 
```
NODE embed-n0: gpu_queue_depth=210 inflight_requests=85 avg_batch=96 kernel_miss=0.42
NODE embed-n1: gpu_queue_depth=180 inflight_requests=74 avg_batch=88 kernel_miss=0.47
```

jordan_sre: kernel_miss ~0.45 indicates fallback kernel or slow path frequently executing. That aligns with large, odd-shaped batches. Two immediate mitigations: (A) temporarily lower BATCH_WINDOW_MS to 8ms for ACME route, (B) route them to fp16 variant open-embed-v2-fp16 as a fallback. I'll apply (A) now and monitor.

engbot: action: set_route_param customer=acme BATCH_WINDOW_MS=8 by jordan_sre at 2025-02-12T08:16:12Z

maya_support: After lowering BATCH_WINDOW_MS, vectors/sec recovered to ~1400 and gpu_queue_depth dropped under 40 within 90s. Customer still asking for root cause and permanent fix.

alex_ml: Next steps to confirm root cause: collect pprof traces and model-server logs around the event, capture request traces for req_5881fa and adjacent request_ids, and examine whether quantized kernel selection differs when batch shapes exceed 64. If we can reproduce locally, we should add a guarded kernel selection or a heuristic to cap max effective batch for quantized path.

eng_oncall: I'll collect the logs. Can you grab these from the customer-facing node: 
```
scp root@embed-n0:/var/log/inference/model-server.log /tmp/acme-embed.log
kubectl exec -n prod embed-n0 -- cat /proc/gpu/queue_stats > /tmp/queue_stats
```

maya_support: Noted. One more wrinkle — their client rotated API keys ~08:10 and we see a short burst of 401s then retries from their side. That likely amplified concurrency and pushed the system into the large-batch slow path. Adding this to the incident notes.

sre_oncall: I'll create a post-incident task: (1) add guardrail to router to detect sudden retry storms and temporarily shrink batch window, (2) add a per-route kernel fallback threshold, (3) notify CustSuccess for rollback guidance. Assigned to eng-runtime and eng-ml.

maya_support: Thanks — I'll coordinate a repro window with ACME and collect requested traces. Will DM req_ ids once available. :thumbsup:
